statement: You are given an integer array nums and an integer k. A subsequence picks any set of positions of nums, keeping their order.

Return the number of subsequences whose elements add up to k. Subsequences are counted by the positions they use, so equal values at different positions give different subsequences. The empty subsequence has sum 0, so it is counted when k = 0.
Solve it with the pick / not-pick recursion: at each index, count the subsequences that include nums[i] and those that skip it, and add the two counts.

examples.explanation: The single 2 is one subsequence, and the two 1s together are another, so the count is 2.
Any two of the four 1s make 2, and there are 4 × 3 / 2 = 6 ways to choose two positions.
